overall_assessment: All 28 packet entries were read in full, including all displayed removed spans; packet truncations limit conclusions about omitted text. Anonymization generally preserves course content and removes approval blocks and semester dating, but two Systems Thinking offerings retain staff names under English role labels; no confirmed personal-data leak or content over-removal was found in the eight random controls. The name_label flags identify this real leak, while the other visible name_like, phone and admin_date signals are consistent with organisations, titles, reference authors, ISBNs and publication or government-document dates; the high removed-share flags reflect legitimate administrative/widget cleanup in short plans rather than confirmed content loss.

findings.evidence: Course Owner: Professor [name] Lecturer: Associate Professor [name]
findings.description: Both Systems Thinking offerings retain the course owner and lecturer by full name in Miscellaneous. These are staff named in their institutional roles, not reference authors or subject-matter figures, and must be removed. This is the same defect in two of the 28 reviewed offerings.
findings.root_cause_hypothesis: R/anonymize.R: .anon_usn() removes approval blocks but has no rule for this English staff line. The generic .staff_roles list omits Course Owner and Lecturer, so .role_name_inline_regex does not recognize either label, even though .title_regex supports Professor and Associate Professor.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a USN rule matching the complete staff-only line beginning Course Owner: and containing Lecturer:, or extend the role-aware generic rules to these exact English labels. Remove both names and their titles while preserving the following programme-guidelines sentence; verify both sampled offerings and ensure literature authors remain unchanged.
